Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes): Soreness and cracking of skin on the hands (palms), with palm-dominant involvement and itch; chronic course (3–4 months) affecting work; generalized dryness noted on legs as well. Known type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Hydration reportedly limited. No fever, nausea, vomiting, or GI/urinary symptoms.
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Family history notable for diabetes.
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Metformin; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Non-smoker; alcohol use around a couple of pints per week; occupational exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent glove use during work; hydration limited.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (based on transcript and DDx alignment): Dermatitis/hand dermatitis with a likely irritant contact component, possible allergic contact dermatitis, and dimensional contribution from xerosis; palm predominant with itching and fissuring.
- Key supporting findings from transcript: Chronic palm involvement with cracking and itching; occupational exposure to cleaning products; intermittent glove use; improvement not achieved with OTC moisturizers; no systemic symptoms.
- Relevant differentials from DDx (supporting or refining impression):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — High likelihood: Occupational exposure to cleaning agents with inconsistent glove use; palmar involvement and chronic course.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Medium-High likelihood: Possible sensitization to cleaning agents; pruritus and fissuring fit dermatitis spectrum.
  - Hand dermatitis/eczema (including potential atopic component) — Medium likelihood: Chronic dry, itchy hands with fissures; may be exacerbated by irritants or allergens.
  - Xerosis with fissuring related to diabetes/metabolic dryness — Medium-Low likelihood: Diabetes-related dry skin possible but palmar inflammation and itching point more toward contact dermatitis.
- Plan:
  - Avoid triggers: Strong recommendation to wear gloves consistently when cleaning; minimize contact with irritants.
  - Topical anti-inflammatory therapy: Prescribe a topical corticosteroid to reduce inflammation.
  - Skin moisturization: Recommend stronger emollients, applied 3–4 times daily, for the next 2 weeks.
  - Follow-up: Recheck in 1–2 weeks; return sooner if spreading, worsening, or not improving.
  - Pharmacy: Prescription to be sent to the patient’s pharmacy.
  - Patient education: Reinforce glove use and skin care routine; discuss hydration and avoidance of aggravating products.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Emphasize protective skin care, glove use to prevent irritant exposure, and appropriate hydration.
- Patient health goals and priorities: Not explicitly recorded; to emphasize return demonstration of skin improvement and reduced exposure to irritants.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Irritant contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Occupational exposure to cleaning products with inconsistent glove use; palm-dominant involvement; itching and fissuring; chronic course consistent with irritant dermatitis.
- Allergic contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Medium-High
  - Justification: Possible sensitization to cleaning agents; pruritus and fissuring; exposure history supports consideration; patch testing could help confirm.
- Hand dermatitis/eczema (including possible atopic component)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Chronic dry, itchy hands with fissures, compatible with eczema phenotype; may be exacerbated by irritants or allergens.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs, immunization status, and basic laboratories not recorded; no age confirmation beyond patient report; no imaging or objective measurements provided.
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: None identified between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality notes: Dialogue provides clear history of hand symptoms with occupational exposure and response to OTC products; no contradictory statements detected.
